analysis.title: GS Coppersmith - US EQUITIES a pulse check 25 Oct 2026
key_insights: The S&P fell less than 50bps on the week and sits 2.5% below its highs, but hedge fund portfolios took heavy losses beneath the surface.

On Thursday, Fundamental L/S, Systematic and Multi-Strats all lost more than 1% on the same day, the first time since COVID. The Hedge Fund VIP long/short basket fell 4%, a move matched over the past decade only by DeepSeek Monday and the COVID selloff.
TMT-focused hedge funds are down 9.6% MTD and Asia Fundamental L/S is down 9.3% MTD.

The desk reads the move as an investor leverage unwind rather than an AI demand bubble bursting. Positioning has moved faster than fundamentals, and investors defended exposures with other positions rather than cutting risk until late last week.

Hedge fund gross leverage was still 312% (96th percentile over five years) after the selling. Fundamental net leverage fell to 47%, a one-year low. Investors are more defensive without having worked down gross exposure, which explains the persistent pain.
The GS floor saw about $20bn of TMT selling over two weeks, close to the $23bn during July's AI unwind. SPX is down 2.4% this time versus 3.4% in July.
AI stocks are moving much more closely together while index volatility stays contained. The desk hopes for a positioning equilibrium similar to July's, after which the market turned positive.
The risk is that discretionary selling gives way to systematic selling. CTAs are long $38.5bn of S&P futures (91st percentile), nearly 80% of aggregate net longs across the 21 markets tracked.
The S&P is below its short-term CTA trend threshold. The medium-term level is about 1.3% below Friday's close.

Modeled CTA flows are asymmetric. They are estimated to sell $11.6bn of S&P over the next week in a flat tape and up to $65bn in a substantial one-month downside scenario. The one-month upside buying scenario is only $9bn, and a 2 SD rally next week still leaves CTAs net sellers.
Nasdaq CTA signals have deteriorated. Russell CTA positioning is heavily short and could force buying on a rally.

SPX volatility is starting to react. Fixed-strike vol is bid, downside skew and tails are outperforming, and VIX positioning and VIX volatility are drawing attention. The Vol Panic Index rose from 4.63 Wednesday to 7.94 Friday, reaching the 'panic' threshold for the first time since late July.

Catalysts this week: Microsoft and Alphabet report Wednesday, Amazon reports Thursday, and the Fed decision is Wednesday. Scrutiny of AI capex, funding needs and returns is higher after META, so the bar for reassurance has risen.

Korea: after a 40% KOSPI correction, GS research cut its 12-month target from 12,000 to 9,000, which still implies more than 60% upside. At 4x forward earnings, much of the memory-cycle bad news is priced in.
Brazil's presidential runoff puts EWZ, the currency and local rates in focus as an alternative to the crowded AI trade.

The desk's bias is a relief rally after two weeks of selling, held loosely given elevated gross exposure, negative systematic flow asymmetry and geopolitical risk. It favors call spreads to express upside with defined downside.
